title: Undefined polar domain
concern: The manuscript uses labels such as Arctic-wide, Antarctic-wide, high-latitude, or Southern Ocean without an operational spatial boundary aligned to the analysis.
evidence_risk: A geographic label can conceal excluded seas, shelves, ice sectors, elevation bands, or latitude zones and make the conclusion impossible to reproduce.
revision_direction: State the exact mask, coordinate reference, sector definitions, exclusions, and sensitivity to alternative accepted regional boundaries.
triggers: Arctic-wide; Antarctic-wide; Southern Ocean; circumpolar

title: Season definition mismatched to process
concern: Calendar seasons are used even though melt, freeze-up, polar night, snow accumulation, or biological timing varies strongly by region and year.
evidence_risk: Fixed seasons can mix different physical regimes and create artificial spatial or temporal contrasts.
revision_direction: Use process-based or locally justified seasonal windows, show robustness to reasonable alternatives, and qualify conclusions that depend on the window.
triggers: DJF; JJA; melt season; freeze-up; polar night

title: Single sector generalized to a hemisphere
concern: Evidence from one basin, shelf, glacier cluster, station network, or transect is presented as representative of the full Arctic or Antarctic.
evidence_risk: Polar sectors differ in circulation, geometry, climate forcing, ecology, and observing density.
revision_direction: Narrow the claim or add stratified evidence across relevant sectors, explicitly testing spatial heterogeneity.
triggers: one sector; one shelf; one basin; circumpolar conclusion

title: Bipolar analogy lacks transfer argument
concern: A mechanism established in one hemisphere is transferred to the other without testing differences in land-ocean geometry, seasonality, circulation, or human context.
evidence_risk: The Arctic and Antarctic are not interchangeable experimental systems.
revision_direction: Identify the transfer assumptions, test them where data permit, and treat the comparison as a hypothesis unless both systems are evaluated.
triggers: Arctic versus Antarctic; bipolar comparison; analog

title: Coastal and interior regimes conflated
concern: Coastal, shelf, marginal-ice-zone, interior plateau, and deep-basin observations are pooled despite distinct forcing and response regimes.
evidence_risk: Pooling can manufacture an average response that is not valid for any physical regime.
revision_direction: Stratify by regime, report interactions or heterogeneity, and avoid a single polar-wide coefficient when slopes differ.
triggers: coastal; interior; shelf; marginal ice zone

title: Study period omits critical phase
concern: The selected interval excludes freeze-up, breakup, winter darkness, shoulder seasons, or an earlier baseline that is necessary to interpret the claimed transition.
evidence_risk: A truncated window can misidentify timing, trend magnitude, or causal order.
revision_direction: Justify temporal coverage, show the full available record, and test conclusions across alternative start and end dates.
triggers: record begins; selected years; summer-only; winter gap

title: Event-year framing mistaken for state change
concern: An extreme year or short cluster is described as a new climatic or ecological state without a defined state metric or persistence criterion.
evidence_risk: Internal variability and transient anomalies can mimic regime change.
revision_direction: Define the state variable and transition criterion, quantify persistence and recurrence, and compare against an appropriate null or historical distribution.
triggers: record low; unprecedented; new state; tipping

title: Map projection and cell area not handled
concern: Area, distance, gradient, or neighborhood calculations are performed in a polar projection without documenting distortion, cell-area weighting, or reprojection effects.
evidence_risk: Unweighted polar grids can bias aggregate statistics and spatial relationships.
revision_direction: Document the projection, use area-aware calculations, and demonstrate that reprojection or latitude weighting does not control the result.
triggers: polar stereographic; grid-cell area; map distance

title: Logistics-driven sampling bias
concern: Sampling is concentrated near stations, ship tracks, air routes, roads, accessible glaciers, or safe summer conditions but treated as population-representative.
evidence_risk: Accessibility is correlated with climate, topography, ecosystem type, and disturbance, creating structured selection bias.
revision_direction: Map the sampling frame, quantify coverage by environmental stratum, use weighting or hierarchical inference, and narrow claims where coverage is absent.
triggers: station; cruise; transect; accessible site; summer campaign

title: Summer observations infer winter process
concern: Warm-season measurements are used to infer winter fluxes, stratification, snow processes, ecology, or atmosphere-surface exchange.
evidence_risk: Polar winter can reverse process direction and is often the least observed season.
revision_direction: Add winter evidence, use a validated seasonal model with uncertainty, or limit the conclusion to the observed season.
triggers: summer campaign; winter process; annual budget

title: Sparse sites support trend estimate
concern: A trend is estimated from a small or changing station network without accounting for spatial covariance, site turnover, and unequal record length.
evidence_risk: Network evolution can be confounded with environmental change.
revision_direction: Report site histories, use methods robust to unbalanced panels and spatial dependence, and test leave-site-out stability.
triggers: monitoring network; station turnover; sparse sites

title: Cruise track treated as synoptic map
concern: Shipboard observations collected over days or weeks are interpreted as a simultaneous spatial field.
evidence_risk: Temporal evolution along the cruise can alias into apparent spatial gradients.
revision_direction: Model or remove temporal drift, use repeat sections or autonomous observations, and report the synoptic limitation.
triggers: cruise track; transect map; spatial gradient

title: Validation sites overlap development sites
concern: The same stations, cores, scenes, transects, or reanalysis-constrained products contribute to algorithm tuning and reported validation.
evidence_risk: Circular validation inflates apparent accuracy and may hide regional failure.
revision_direction: Create a genuinely independent holdout by site, period, sensor, or region and disclose all data dependencies.
triggers: calibration and validation; training sites; cross-validation

title: Biological samples ignore habitat structure
concern: Ecological samples are pooled across ice edge, open water, under-ice, benthic, stream, or terrestrial habitats without a design that represents their area and season.
evidence_risk: Habitat imbalance can be mistaken for a climate or ice effect.
revision_direction: Use stratified sampling or multilevel models, report habitat-specific effects, and weight only with defensible habitat prevalence.
triggers: microbiome; food web; ice edge; habitat

title: Core or archive is spatially overinterpreted
concern: One sediment core, lake, or ice core is used to infer regional climate without demonstrating source area and replication.
evidence_risk: Local catchment, accumulation, advection, and post-depositional effects may dominate the record.
revision_direction: Constrain the source footprint, compare independent nearby archives, and state the spatial scale actually supported.
triggers: single core; lake sediment; ice core; regional climate

title: Missingness assumed random
concern: Cloud, darkness, instrument failure, unsafe conditions, melt contamination, or inaccessible terrain creates missing data that are treated as random.
evidence_risk: Polar missingness often depends on the environmental state being estimated.
revision_direction: Characterize missingness by state and season, use sensitivity bounds or explicit observation models, and avoid unconditional interpolation.
triggers: cloud gap; polar night; missing scenes; instrument outage

title: Sea-ice metrics are interchanged
concern: Sea-ice concentration, area, extent, thickness, volume, age, and duration are discussed as if they measured the same system property.
evidence_risk: Different metrics respond to different processes and thresholds and cannot support identical trend or mechanism claims.
revision_direction: Define every metric and threshold, preserve units and denominators, and align the claim with the measured quantity.
triggers: sea ice extent; area; concentration; thickness; volume

title: Elevation change equated with mass change
concern: Surface-elevation change is interpreted as ice mass change without separating density, firn compaction, snow variability, floating geometry, or dynamic effects.
evidence_risk: Height-to-mass conversion can dominate the inferred signal.
revision_direction: State the density and firn assumptions, propagate them, distinguish grounded and floating ice, and compare an independent mass estimate.
triggers: altimetry; elevation change; mass loss

title: Glacier retreat equated with mass loss
concern: Terminus position, area loss, calving-front retreat, frontal ablation, thinning, and total mass balance are conflated.
evidence_risk: A glacier can retreat without proportional mass loss and vice versa.
revision_direction: Use precise glacier-change variables, report geometry and mass components separately, and revise causal language.
triggers: terminus retreat; area change; mass loss; calving

title: Permafrost indicators are conflated
concern: Ground temperature, active-layer thickness, permafrost extent, ground-ice loss, thermokarst, subsidence, and carbon release are treated as interchangeable thaw indicators.
evidence_risk: Each variable reflects a different process, depth, and response time.
revision_direction: Define the measured state variable, depth and season; avoid translating one indicator into another without a validated model.
triggers: permafrost warming; thaw; active layer; subsidence

title: Surface mass balance and total balance mixed
concern: Accumulation and surface ablation are combined conceptually with ice discharge, basal melt, or calving when interpreting ice-sheet or glacier mass balance.
evidence_risk: Mispartitioning obscures the mechanism and can reverse attribution.
revision_direction: Report each budget component and sign convention, identify residual terms, and use total mass balance only when all relevant components are included.
triggers: surface mass balance; discharge; basal melt; total balance

title: Proxy target changes across calibration
concern: A proxy is calibrated to one environmental variable but interpreted as another, such as temperature to circulation strength or sediment composition to storminess.
evidence_risk: Non-unique proxy controls undermine the reconstructed quantity.
revision_direction: Specify the mechanistic proxy chain, test competing controls, and calibrate against the claimed target at matching scale.
triggers: proxy; calibration; reconstruction; interpretation

title: Products with different definitions are merged
concern: Time series from products using different masks, thresholds, sensors, retrieval targets, or version conventions are concatenated without harmonization.
evidence_risk: An apparent trend or discontinuity may be a product-definition artifact.
revision_direction: Document definitions and versions, quantify inter-product offsets, and construct a homogenized record or analyze products separately.
triggers: multi-product; version; merged record; threshold

title: Freshwater, meltwater, and runoff are mixed
concern: Ice melt, snowmelt, liquid precipitation, subglacial discharge, runoff, and net freshwater flux are used interchangeably.
evidence_risk: The terms have different source regions, timing, routing, and budget implications.
revision_direction: Partition sources and pathways, state the control volume, and use terminology consistent with the measured or modeled flux.
triggers: freshwater flux; meltwater; runoff; discharge

title: Retrieval product treated as direct truth
concern: A satellite retrieval is used as a direct observation without describing algorithm assumptions, flags, known failure modes, or product uncertainty.
evidence_risk: The retrieval may be conditional on surface state, atmosphere, snow, roughness, or training data.
revision_direction: Cite the exact product version and algorithm documentation, apply quality flags, and propagate retrieval uncertainty into the main result.
triggers: satellite product; retrieval; direct observation; quality flag

title: Melt ponds and wet snow bias sea-ice retrieval
concern: Summer sea-ice concentration or type is interpreted without testing melt-pond, wet-snow, atmospheric, and thin-ice ambiguity.
evidence_risk: Surface-state changes can appear as ice loss or category change.
revision_direction: Use season-appropriate products, compare independent sensors or algorithms, and bound the effect of surface-state ambiguity.
triggers: melt pond; wet snow; passive microwave; summer ice

title: Sensor transition creates artificial trend
concern: A long record spans missions, processing streams, or orbit changes without an explicit homogeneity assessment.
evidence_risk: Instrument and algorithm transitions can generate steps comparable to the climate trend.
revision_direction: Perform overlap calibration, breakpoint tests, product intercomparison, and sensitivity to transition treatment.
triggers: sensor transition; mission change; climate data record

title: Polar gap or coverage mask is ignored
concern: Orbit geometry, pole holes, cloud screening, darkness, topographic shadow, or coastal masks exclude nonrandom parts of the domain.
evidence_risk: Coverage gaps may bias totals, trend maps, and event timing.
revision_direction: Show coverage through time, distinguish observed from infilled cells, and test conclusions under conservative gap treatments.
triggers: pole hole; cloud mask; polar night; coverage

title: Spatial resolution cannot resolve mechanism
concern: The product grid or radar footprint is too coarse to resolve grounding zones, narrow fjords, leads, small glaciers, thermokarst features, or coastal gradients invoked in the mechanism.
evidence_risk: Subpixel mixing and geolocation uncertainty can determine the signal.
revision_direction: Demonstrate scale compatibility, aggregate the claim to resolvable scales, or add higher-resolution evidence.
triggers: resolution; subpixel; grounding line; fjord; lead

title: Radar interpretation lacks dielectric alternatives
concern: Radar backscatter, interferometric phase, attenuation, or reflectors are assigned to water, brine, layer geometry, or damage without excluding other dielectric and geometric causes.
evidence_risk: The same radar signature can have multiple physical origins.
revision_direction: Use multi-frequency, temporal, geometric, or in situ constraints and present the interpretation as conditional where alternatives remain.
triggers: radar; InSAR; reflector; seawater intrusion

title: Validation scale mismatches product scale
concern: Point or transect field measurements are compared directly with large grid cells or temporally averaged products.
evidence_risk: Representativeness error can dominate the apparent product bias.
revision_direction: Upscale field data with a defensible model, sample the grid footprint, and separate measurement from representativeness uncertainty.
triggers: ground truth; grid cell; footprint; validation

title: Algorithm comparison is not independent
concern: Products compared as independent evidence share sensors, weather filters, ancillary fields, training data, or common retrieval heritage.
evidence_risk: Agreement among dependent products overstates confidence.
revision_direction: Map data lineage, select genuinely independent observations where possible, and qualify ensemble agreement by shared dependencies.
triggers: product ensemble; independent products; shared input

title: Budget does not close
concern: The central mass, heat, freshwater, carbon, or energy budget omits material terms or leaves an unexplained residual.
evidence_risk: A mechanism claim is weak when the accounting cannot reproduce the observed tendency.
revision_direction: Define the control volume and sign convention, report every term and residual, and propagate uncertainty into closure.
triggers: budget closure; residual; conservation; control volume

title: Grounded and floating ice are mixed
concern: Mass or melt changes on ice shelves and floating tongues are combined with grounded-ice loss when discussing sea-level contribution.
evidence_risk: Floating-ice melt has different direct sea-level implications and dynamic pathways.
revision_direction: Separate grounded and floating domains, state grounding-line masks, and quantify dynamic effects rather than implying direct equivalence.
triggers: ice shelf; floating tongue; grounded ice; sea level

title: Firn and density assumptions dominate conversion
concern: Volume or height changes are converted to mass with fixed density or insufficient firn treatment.
evidence_risk: Snow accumulation, compaction, meltwater retention, and density variability can create spurious mass trends.
revision_direction: Use a validated firn/density model, show sensitivity and uncertainty, and compare against an independent gravimetric or input-output estimate.
triggers: firn; density; altimetry; mass conversion

title: Snow depth uncertainty omitted from sea-ice thickness
concern: Freeboard-derived thickness is reported without propagating snow depth, snow density, ice density, and hydrostatic assumptions.
evidence_risk: Snow uncertainty can dominate sea-ice thickness and volume estimates.
revision_direction: Report the full uncertainty chain, test alternative snow products, and avoid overprecise volume trends.
triggers: freeboard; snow depth; sea ice thickness; hydrostatic

title: Freshwater routing lacks travel-time treatment
concern: Melt or subglacial discharge is linked to downstream ocean, ice-shelf, or ecosystem response without resolving storage, routing, mixing, and lag.
evidence_risk: Coincident timing does not establish the proposed pathway.
revision_direction: Constrain travel times and pathways with observations or process models and test alternative timing assumptions.
triggers: subglacial discharge; meltwater routing; lag

title: Surface energy terms are incompletely constrained
concern: Melt or freeze is attributed to one flux while radiation, turbulent fluxes, rain heat, ocean heat, albedo, or conductive storage are omitted or weakly observed.
evidence_risk: A partial energy budget cannot distinguish mechanisms.
revision_direction: Close the energy budget at the relevant temporal scale, report flux uncertainty, and test whether the proposed term explains residual variability.
triggers: surface energy balance; melt; turbulent flux; albedo

title: Carbon inventory and flux are confused
concern: Concentration, inventory, production, oxidation, evasion, and net ecosystem or ocean-atmosphere flux are interpreted interchangeably.
evidence_risk: A large pool does not imply a large net emission or uptake.
revision_direction: Separate stocks and gross/net fluxes, define the integration domain and period, and support source-sink attribution with a closed budget.
triggers: carbon uptake; methane emission; inventory; flux

title: Unresolved basal melt parameterization controls result
concern: Ice-shelf or ice-sheet response is driven by prescribed basal melt without showing sensitivity to calibration, geometry, cavity circulation, or climate forcing.
evidence_risk: The headline projection may be a parameterization artifact.
revision_direction: Report calibration data and parameter ranges, run structural alternatives, and separate robust conclusions from parameterization-dependent outcomes.
triggers: basal melt; ISMIP6; parameterization; ice shelf

title: Grid cannot represent key geometry
concern: Model resolution is too coarse for grounding zones, shelf channels, narrow straits, fjords, leads, steep terrain, or polygonal permafrost invoked in the explanation.
evidence_risk: Unresolved geometry can change transport, stress, melt, and feedback direction.
revision_direction: Demonstrate convergence or use parameterizations validated for the target scale; limit mechanistic claims when the feature is unresolved.
triggers: grid resolution; geometry; fjord; grounding line; channel

title: Boundary conditions encode the result
concern: Ocean, atmosphere, basal, geothermal, bed, or ecological boundary conditions are prescribed in a way that already imposes the claimed response.
evidence_risk: The simulation may illustrate an assumption rather than independently test a mechanism.
revision_direction: Identify which conclusions follow from boundary choices, run alternative plausible conditions, and avoid causal language unsupported by sensitivity.
triggers: boundary condition; forcing; prescribed; scenario

title: Assimilation product used as independent validation
concern: A reanalysis or assimilated product is used both to force or constrain the model and to validate its performance.
evidence_risk: Shared observations and model structure make the validation circular.
revision_direction: Use withheld observations or an independent product, disclose assimilation lineage, and separate fit to constraints from predictive skill.
triggers: reanalysis; data assimilation; validation; forcing

title: Single model presented as structural certainty
concern: A result from one model, one configuration, or one parameterization is presented as a robust system response.
evidence_risk: Polar projections are often sensitive to unresolved processes and model structure.
revision_direction: Use a multi-model or structural ensemble, perturb key process choices, and label model-contingent results.
triggers: single model; structural uncertainty; projection

title: Ensemble members are not independent
concern: Initial-condition members or models sharing code and parameterizations are treated as independent samples when estimating probability.
evidence_risk: Effective sample size is smaller than the nominal ensemble and tails are poorly constrained.
revision_direction: Describe ensemble dependence, estimate effective sample size, and avoid precise event probabilities unsupported by the ensemble design.
triggers: ensemble; probability; independent members; CMIP

title: Tuning and evaluation periods overlap
concern: Parameters are selected using the same period, event, or site used to claim predictive accuracy or mechanism fidelity.
evidence_risk: Overfitting can be severe in short polar records.
revision_direction: Separate calibration and evaluation by time and region, report pre-specified metrics, and test out-of-sample stability.
triggers: calibration; tuning; hindcast; validation period

title: Subgrid scheme lacks scale-aware validation
concern: A subgrid process such as leads, melt ponds, snow redistribution, calving, drainage, or thermokarst is parameterized without validation across the operating range.
evidence_risk: A tuned average behavior may fail under changing climate or geometry.
revision_direction: Validate the scheme against process observations, test extrapolation, and report when the result depends on the closure.
triggers: subgrid; parameterization; melt pond; calving; drainage

title: Scenario spread is mistaken for forecast uncertainty
concern: A selected scenario set or forcing range is presented as the full uncertainty distribution.
evidence_risk: Scenario, internal-variability, parameter, observational, and structural uncertainties are distinct.
revision_direction: Decompose uncertainty sources and state whether results are conditional projections, scenarios, hindcasts, or forecasts.
triggers: scenario; projection; forecast; uncertainty range

title: Correlation is promoted to mechanism
concern: Covariation between sea ice, circulation, ocean heat, ecology, or greenhouse-gas flux is described as a causal process without discriminating evidence.
evidence_risk: Common forcing, autocorrelation, or feedback can produce the same association.
revision_direction: Specify causal alternatives, use temporal or intervention-like evidence where possible, and calibrate language to association unless alternatives are excluded.
triggers: correlation; drives; controls; mechanism; feedback

title: Internal variability is underrepresented
concern: A short trend or extreme event is attributed to external forcing without estimating variability from observations, large ensembles, or physically appropriate null models.
evidence_risk: Polar variability is large and serially correlated.
revision_direction: Quantify the expected distribution under internal variability, test sensitivity to trend window, and express attribution probabilistically.
triggers: attribution; internal variability; trend; extreme

title: Feedback direction is not identified
concern: Coupled variables are interpreted as a one-way driver-response relation although reciprocal feedbacks are plausible.
evidence_risk: The sign and timing of a feedback cannot be inferred from contemporaneous correlation.
revision_direction: Use lagged/process evidence, perturbation experiments, or budget analysis to distinguish direction; otherwise present a coupled association.
triggers: feedback; coupling; lag; sea ice-ocean-atmosphere

title: Teleconnection pathway is incomplete
concern: A remote climate mode is linked to a polar response without closing the dynamical pathway or testing competing modes and seasonality.
evidence_risk: Shared trends and mode covariance can produce unstable attribution.
revision_direction: Demonstrate the circulation pathway, test multivariate and detrended alternatives, and evaluate stability across periods or models.
triggers: teleconnection; oscillation; circulation; Arctic response

title: Historical relationship assumed stationary
concern: An empirical climate, ecological, or proxy relationship is extrapolated into a regime with changing ice cover, stratification, species composition, or atmospheric moisture.
evidence_risk: The predictor-response relation may change as the system reorganizes.
revision_direction: Test time-varying parameters or regime interactions, diagnose extrapolation, and restrict forecasts to supported conditions.
triggers: nonstationary; future projection; empirical relationship

title: Process timing is inconsistent with causation
concern: The proposed driver does not precede the response at a physically plausible lag or the analysis averages away the relevant sequence.
evidence_risk: Causal interpretation requires temporal ordering and compatible response times.
revision_direction: Analyze event chronology and lags, compare alternative pathways, and revise the mechanism if timing is inconsistent.
triggers: lag; timing; immediate response; seasonal sequence

title: Counterfactual is not defined
concern: Terms such as anthropogenic contribution, policy benefit, tipping avoidance, or avoided warming are used without an explicit counterfactual experiment.
evidence_risk: Attribution and intervention claims depend on what would have occurred otherwise.
revision_direction: Define the counterfactual, justify forcing differences, quantify uncertainty, and separate scenario comparison from formal attribution.
triggers: counterfactual; policy; anthropogenic; avoided warming

title: Mechanism depends on one diagnostic
concern: A broad process conclusion rests on a single index, composite, regression coefficient, or model diagnostic.
evidence_risk: A diagnostic may be consistent with multiple mechanisms and sensitive to definition.
revision_direction: Add convergent process evidence, test alternative diagnostics, and state which mechanism components remain inferred.
triggers: index; composite; regression; diagnostic

title: Serial and spatial dependence ignored
concern: Significance tests treat polar time series, pixels, stations, or model cells as independent.
evidence_risk: Autocorrelation and spatial covariance inflate effective sample size and apparent certainty.
revision_direction: Use dependence-aware uncertainty, report effective sample size, and test robustness across correlation models.
triggers: p value; pixels; time series; spatial autocorrelation

title: Uncertainty is not propagated to headline result
concern: Input, calibration, retrieval, age-model, density, forcing, or parameter uncertainties are listed but not propagated to the final trend, budget, or projection.
evidence_risk: The headline confidence can be much narrower than the evidence supports.
revision_direction: Propagate all material uncertainty sources, including covariance, and report their contribution to the final interval.
triggers: uncertainty propagation; error budget; confidence interval

title: Sensitivity tests do not span plausible choices
concern: Robustness is claimed from a narrow set of thresholds, windows, products, priors, or model parameters selected near the preferred analysis.
evidence_risk: A local perturbation does not test structural uncertainty.
revision_direction: Predefine a plausible sensitivity space, include alternative products and methods, and show which conclusions survive.
triggers: sensitivity; threshold; window; parameter choice

title: Multiple comparisons are unaccounted
concern: Large spatial, temporal, taxonomic, or parameter searches report selected significant patterns without multiplicity or selection correction.
evidence_risk: False discoveries are likely and effect sizes may be inflated.
revision_direction: Control the false-discovery process or use hierarchical models, report the search space, and validate selected patterns independently.
triggers: many pixels; many species; field significance; screening

title: Rare-event probability is overprecise
concern: The date or probability of an ice-free day, tipping event, extreme melt, or circulation threshold is estimated from too few effective samples.
evidence_risk: Tail probabilities are highly sensitive to model dependence, threshold definition, and distributional assumptions.
revision_direction: Report interval and threshold sensitivity, effective sample size, and conditional probability wording rather than a precise deterministic date.
triggers: first event; return period; tipping probability; before 2030

title: Cross-validation leaks space or time
concern: Random splits place neighboring pixels, repeated sites, adjacent years, or derived samples in both train and test sets.
evidence_risk: The evaluation measures interpolation rather than geographic or temporal transfer.
revision_direction: Use blocked spatial and temporal validation, hold out entire sites or regions, and report out-of-domain performance.
triggers: random split; machine learning; cross-validation; spatial leakage

title: Baseline comparison is weak or mismatched
concern: A new method or model is compared with an outdated, differently forced, differently resolved, or insufficiently tuned baseline.
evidence_risk: Apparent improvement may result from unequal information or setup.
revision_direction: Use strong matched baselines, harmonize inputs and evaluation domains, and report uncertainty in performance differences.
triggers: benchmark; baseline; model comparison; skill

title: Confidence language exceeds validation domain
concern: The manuscript claims robustness, ubiquity, prediction, or early warning despite narrow data, one event, or an in-sample fit.
evidence_risk: Statistical confidence within the sampled domain does not establish external validity.
revision_direction: Separate in-domain precision from transfer uncertainty and align language with the actual validation design.
triggers: robust; pervasive; predicts; early warning

title: Grounding-line location uncertainty omitted
concern: Grounding-line migration or retreat is central, but the mapping method, tidal state, hydrostatic assumption, and positional uncertainty are not quantified.
evidence_risk: Small positional errors can alter inferred retreat rate and process attribution.
revision_direction: Describe the detection method, provide uncertainty and tidal sensitivity, and compare independent observations where available.
triggers: grounding line; migration; retreat; tidal flexure

title: Calving attribution ignores geometry and stress history
concern: A calving event is attributed to climate forcing without considering rift history, pinning points, mélange, geometry, and preconditioning.
evidence_risk: Calving can be a delayed geometric instability rather than an immediate climate response.
revision_direction: Reconstruct stress and geometry evolution, test alternative triggers, and distinguish event timing from long-term forcing.
triggers: calving; rift; ice shelf; geometry

title: Ocean-temperature metric is not dynamically relevant
concern: Offshore, depth-averaged, or sparse temperature is used as the forcing for glacier or ice-shelf melt without demonstrating access to the ice interface.
evidence_risk: Circulation, bathymetry, stratification, and mixing control heat delivery.
revision_direction: Use cavity or fjord-relevant thermal forcing, demonstrate pathways, and quantify lag and transport uncertainty.
triggers: ocean warming; thermal forcing; cavity; fjord

title: Bed or bathymetry uncertainty is underexplored
concern: Conclusions about stability, retreat, or melt depend on poorly resolved bed or seafloor geometry.
evidence_risk: Geometry uncertainty can change circulation, grounding-line stability, and stress transmission.
revision_direction: Propagate alternative bed/bathymetry realizations and identify conclusions that remain robust.
triggers: bed topography; bathymetry; seafloor roughness; stability

title: Dynamic and climatic mass loss are not separated
concern: Observed retreat or thinning is attributed to atmospheric or oceanic forcing without separating dynamic adjustment, calving, surface balance, and basal melt.
evidence_risk: Different mechanisms imply different persistence and projections.
revision_direction: Partition components using independent observations or models and calibrate attribution to what can be resolved.
triggers: dynamic thinning; surface balance; basal melt; calving

title: Ice-shelf buttressing claim lacks stress evidence
concern: Loss or thinning of floating ice is assumed to increase grounded-ice discharge without quantifying buttressing or stress transfer.
evidence_risk: Not all floating ice exerts the same dynamic control.
revision_direction: Calculate buttressing or stress sensitivity and identify the grounded catchments dynamically connected to the change.
triggers: buttressing; ice shelf loss; grounded discharge

title: Glacier inventory changes through time
concern: Trend analysis mixes glacier outlines, merges/splits, surge states, or inclusion criteria across epochs.
evidence_risk: Inventory inconsistency can generate artificial area and retreat trends.
revision_direction: Use a stable inventory or document lineage, treat surge-type glaciers separately, and quantify mapping uncertainty.
triggers: glacier inventory; outline; surge; retreat trend

title: Tipping language lacks state-space evidence
concern: Abrupt past or modeled change is labeled a tipping point without demonstrating multiple states, hysteresis, threshold behavior, or self-sustaining change.
evidence_risk: Rapid response alone is not evidence of tipping dynamics.
revision_direction: Define the tipping criterion, test hysteresis or recovery, and use calibrated language if only abrupt change is established.
triggers: tipping point; threshold; hysteresis; irreversible

title: Ice-free threshold is not explicit
concern: An ice-free Arctic, ice-free day, or seasonal loss is discussed without a concentration, extent, area, region, or duration threshold.
evidence_risk: Event timing and probability depend strongly on the operational definition.
revision_direction: Define the metric and threshold before analysis and report sensitivity to accepted alternatives.
triggers: ice-free; threshold; first day; September minimum

title: Wind stress transfer ignores ice mechanics
concern: Surface stress or ocean spin-up is linked to sea-ice loss without resolving internal ice stress, concentration, thickness, drag, and seasonal regime.
evidence_risk: The same wind can transfer different momentum depending on ice state and rheology.
revision_direction: Diagnose the full momentum budget and test sensitivity to drag and rheology choices.
triggers: wind stress; ice weakening; ocean spin-up; drag

title: Sea-ice effect on stratification lacks competing freshwater controls
concern: Winter stratification or carbon uptake is attributed to sea ice without separating brine rejection, meltwater, river input, precipitation, mixing, and advection.
evidence_risk: Several freshwater and mixing pathways can create the same stratification signal.
revision_direction: Close the salinity and mixing budget and test whether the sea-ice pathway is uniquely supported.
triggers: stratification; brine; freshwater; carbon uptake

title: Biological-pump response is inferred from proxies alone
concern: Export or carbon sequestration is inferred from production, community composition, sediment traps, or model diagnostics without closing remineralization and export pathways.
evidence_risk: Higher production does not necessarily increase long-term export.
revision_direction: Measure or constrain export efficiency, remineralization, depth horizon, and seasonal integration; narrow the claim if only production changes are shown.
triggers: biological pump; export; productivity; carbon sequestration

title: Marginal ice zone migration confounds trend
concern: Ecological or oceanographic differences are attributed to ice decline although sampling follows a moving ice edge or habitat boundary.
evidence_risk: The comparison may substitute different water masses or habitats rather than track change at fixed conditions.
revision_direction: Use a coordinate system relative to both geography and ice edge, and separate habitat relocation from temporal change.
triggers: marginal ice zone; ice edge; transect; habitat shift

title: Atmospheric-river detection is algorithm-dependent
concern: Future atmospheric-river frequency or impact is assessed with one detection threshold or tracking algorithm in a changing moisture climate.
evidence_risk: Fixed thresholds can convert thermodynamic moistening into artificial frequency change.
revision_direction: Compare absolute and relative thresholds, multiple algorithms, and impact-based diagnostics; report algorithm dependence.
triggers: atmospheric river; detection threshold; Antarctica

title: Sea-ice state change inferred without process consistency
concern: A new state or regime is declared from low extent alone without consistent evidence in thickness, seasonality, circulation, persistence, or restoring behavior.
evidence_risk: One metric may reflect an extreme realization rather than system reorganization.
revision_direction: Define the state vector, test persistence and multivariate consistency, and compare with internal-variability ensembles.
triggers: new sea ice state; regime shift; record low

title: Ocean circulation proxy is non-unique
concern: Sediment, grain-size, geochemical, or water-mass proxies are interpreted as current strength without excluding source, productivity, preservation, or frontal-position effects.
evidence_risk: Multiple processes can alter the proxy independently of transport.
revision_direction: Use a multi-proxy calibration and model/modern constraints, and distinguish current strength from related water-mass changes.
triggers: ACC strength; circulation proxy; sediment; water mass

title: Ground-temperature trend is generalized to degradation
concern: A temperature increase at boreholes is described as widespread thaw, ground-ice loss, or landscape collapse without corresponding state observations.
evidence_risk: Thermal response and physical degradation differ by depth, ice content, hydrology, and substrate.
revision_direction: Report depth-specific temperatures and add active-layer, deformation, or ground-ice evidence before claiming degradation.
triggers: ground temperature; thaw; degradation; borehole

title: Model permafrost process is not benchmarked
concern: A land model produces permafrost extent or carbon feedback without testing snow insulation, soil physics, organic layers, hydrology, and excess ice.
evidence_risk: Compensating errors can match temperature while misrepresenting process and future response.
revision_direction: Benchmark process diagnostics against observations and perturb structural choices, not only bulk extent.
triggers: CMIP6; land model; soil physics; permafrost

title: Carbon release is inferred from thaw extent
concern: Projected thaw area or active-layer deepening is translated directly into carbon or methane emissions.
evidence_risk: Emission depends on substrate, hydrology, redox state, microbial processing, transport, and oxidation.
revision_direction: Use process-resolving carbon evidence, separate potential stock from realized flux, and report pathway uncertainty.
triggers: permafrost carbon; methane; thaw extent; active layer

title: Microbiome model extrapolates beyond sampled systems
concern: A predictive ecological model trained on accessible glacier-fed streams is applied globally without covering climate, geology, hydrology, and biogeographic domains.
evidence_risk: Out-of-domain ecological prediction can be confidently wrong.
revision_direction: Map environmental coverage, use leave-region-out validation, quantify extrapolation, and limit global claims to supported domains.
triggers: global microbiome; glacier-fed stream; prediction

title: Community composition is equated with ecosystem function
concern: Taxonomic or gene-marker shifts are interpreted as changes in productivity, export, greenhouse-gas cycling, or resilience without functional measurement.
evidence_risk: Composition does not uniquely determine realized process rates.
revision_direction: Add rate or functional assays, triangulate with biogeochemistry, and calibrate functional language.
triggers: community composition; function; microbiome; productivity

title: Freshwater methane filter lacks system boundary
concern: Oxidation or filtering efficiency is interpreted as a fixed ecosystem property without testing residence time, stratification, oxygen, transport, and seasonality.
evidence_risk: A high local oxidation fraction may not predict net annual emission under changing hydrology.
revision_direction: Define the control volume and period, quantify gross production, oxidation, storage, and evasion, and test warming-induced transport changes.
triggers: methane filter; oxidation; freshwater emission; warming

title: Ice-loss effect confounded by co-varying drivers
concern: Ecological change attributed to sea-ice or glacier loss is not separated from temperature, nutrients, light, freshwater, turbidity, habitat, and circulation.
evidence_risk: Co-varying climate drivers can produce a spurious single-driver narrative.
revision_direction: Use experiments, natural gradients, mediation, or process models to discriminate drivers and report unresolved confounding.
triggers: sea ice loss; glacier retreat; ecosystem response

title: Ecological baseline is shifting or incomplete
concern: A short modern baseline is treated as undisturbed or representative despite rapid warming, harvest, pollution, or earlier cryosphere change.
evidence_risk: Effect size and novelty depend on the reference state.
revision_direction: Justify the baseline with historical, paleo, or long-term data and show sensitivity to alternative reference periods.
triggers: baseline; pristine; historical state; rapid change

title: Age uncertainty is omitted from phase relation
concern: Lead-lag, synchrony, abruptness, or event duration is interpreted without propagating age-model uncertainty and correlation between dated levels.
evidence_risk: Chronological uncertainty may be larger than the claimed lag.
revision_direction: Use age ensembles, propagate correlated age uncertainty, and report whether phase conclusions survive.
triggers: age model; lead lag; synchronization; chronology

title: Proxy calibration is outside its environmental range
concern: A modern calibration is applied to glacial, interglacial, or polar conditions with different ecology, chemistry, seasonality, or preservation.
evidence_risk: The transfer function may not be stable outside the calibration domain.
revision_direction: Show calibration coverage, test nonstationarity and alternative proxies, and report extrapolation uncertainty.
triggers: transfer function; calibration range; proxy; glacial

title: Post-depositional alteration is underconstrained
concern: Ice-core isotope, aerosol, gas, snow, or sediment signals are interpreted as direct climate records without quantifying diffusion, wind redistribution, melt, bioturbation, or chemical alteration.
evidence_risk: Archive formation can filter, shift, or erase the environmental signal.
revision_direction: Model or measure post-depositional processes and state the temporal and amplitude resolution retained by the archive.
triggers: post-depositional; diffusion; wind redistribution; isotope

title: Sampling resolution cannot resolve claimed event
concern: The archive sampling interval, smoothing, sedimentation, diffusion, or dating precision is too coarse for the event duration being inferred.
evidence_risk: An unresolved event cannot be used to establish absence, timing, or abruptness.
revision_direction: Quantify the effective resolution, use forward-model tests, and narrow event-scale claims.
triggers: sampling resolution; abrupt event; ice core; sediment core

title: Single proxy is assigned a unique mechanism
concern: One geochemical, isotopic, sedimentological, or biological proxy is interpreted as a unique temperature, storm, circulation, or ice-cover signal.
evidence_risk: Most proxies have multiple environmental and depositional controls.
revision_direction: Use independent proxies and process calibration to discriminate controls; present residual ambiguity explicitly.
triggers: single proxy; temperature; storminess; circulation

title: Core synchronization is circular
concern: Records are aligned using the same climatic feature whose simultaneity or propagation is then claimed.
evidence_risk: Tuning can manufacture apparent synchrony and suppress age uncertainty.
revision_direction: Use independent tie points where possible and repeat the analysis across untuned age ensembles.
triggers: synchronization; tuning; tie point; simultaneous

title: Past threshold is transferred directly to future
concern: A paleoclimate transition is used as a quantitative future threshold without accounting for different forcing rates, geometry, boundary conditions, and initial states.
evidence_risk: Analogues constrain possibilities but may not predict a modern threshold.
revision_direction: Separate qualitative analogue evidence from quantitative projection and test transfer with process models.
triggers: past analogue; future tipping; Last Interglacial

title: Source area and transport change over time
concern: A sediment or aerosol proxy assumes a fixed source although fronts, winds, currents, erosion, and catchment routing may shift.
evidence_risk: Changing provenance can mimic changes in the target climate variable.
revision_direction: Use provenance tracers, transport modeling, and sensitivity to source-area change.
triggers: provenance; sediment source; transport; proxy

title: Indigenous knowledge is treated as extractable data
concern: Community or Indigenous knowledge is incorporated without evidence of appropriate governance, consent, attribution, benefit, or interpretive authority.
evidence_risk: Knowledge use can be scientifically invalid and ethically harmful when detached from its holders and context.
revision_direction: Describe co-design and governance, permissions, data stewardship, attribution, benefits, and limits on reuse; involve relevant knowledge holders in interpretation.
triggers: Indigenous knowledge; traditional knowledge; community data

title: Community relevance is claimed without participation
concern: The paper makes claims about Arctic community needs, impacts, adaptation, or policy without meaningful participation by affected communities.
evidence_risk: Researcher-defined relevance may misrepresent priorities and consequences.
revision_direction: Document engagement and co-production or narrow the claim to biophysical findings without asserting community relevance.
triggers: community impact; adaptation; local relevance; Arctic residents

title: Sensitive location data are released without safeguards
concern: Coordinates or ecological, cultural, archaeological, subsistence, or protected-species data are shared without a sensitivity assessment.
evidence_risk: Open release can create harm, disturbance, or loss of community control.
revision_direction: Apply appropriate access controls, aggregate or redact locations, and document governance decisions.
triggers: sensitive coordinates; sacred site; harvesting; protected species

title: Antarctic protected-area or permit context is absent
concern: Research in or affecting protected areas, fauna, flora, or regulated sampling does not report relevant authorization or management-plan compliance.
evidence_risk: Missing compliance information can undermine legality, reproducibility, and environmental interpretation.
revision_direction: Report permits and area status where applicable, describe compliance and impacts, and avoid legal conclusions beyond the evidence.
triggers: ASPA; permit; Antarctic sampling; protected area

title: Research disturbance is not considered
concern: Field installation, drilling, sampling, wildlife approach, tracer release, vehicle use, or repeated visitation may alter the system being measured.
evidence_risk: The method can create local contamination, disturbance, or behavioral response.
revision_direction: Assess and minimize disturbance, describe controls and permits, and discuss whether the signal could be method-induced.
triggers: drilling; sampling; wildlife; tracer; field installation

title: Policy recommendation exceeds evidence
concern: A local, model-conditional, or observational result is translated into broad mitigation, conservation, shipping, or governance advice without decision analysis.
evidence_risk: Scientific association alone does not establish policy effectiveness, feasibility, distributional effects, or trade-offs.
revision_direction: Separate scientific findings from normative recommendations, define the decision context, and state evidence and uncertainty required for policy claims.
triggers: policy; mitigation; management; governance recommendation

title: Data sovereignty and authorship are unexplained
concern: Community-generated, national-program, expedition, or long-term monitoring data are used without clear stewardship, contributor recognition, or reuse terms.
evidence_risk: Scientific reproducibility does not override legitimate governance and contribution rights.
revision_direction: Document data agreements, access conditions, contributor roles, and attribution; follow community and programme requirements.
triggers: data sovereignty; authorship; monitoring programme; expedition data

title: Compliance review is presented as legal advice
concern: The manuscript or review infers that a project is legally compliant or noncompliant from incomplete reporting.
evidence_risk: Scientific reviewers are not a substitute for competent national authorities or legal review.
revision_direction: Flag missing documentation as a research-reporting risk and request authoritative confirmation rather than making a legal determination.
triggers: legal compliance; permit validity; treaty requirement
